title: Fotografía de Objetos Vintage con Texto Tallado y Pintado Físicamente Integrado
prompt: A hyper-realistic product photography scene featuring vintage nostalgic objects with physically integrated text carved, painted, or etched directly onto their surfaces. TEXT PRESENTATION STYLE: Physical engraved or painted text that is part of the object itself - scratched engraving on object surface creating grooved letters with rough edges, handwritten marker text painted directly on the object with visible ink bleed and brush strokes, faded text on old weathered stickers or labels showing wear and peeling edges, chalk or white paint text written on wooden surfaces with powdery texture and uneven application, rust-stained engraved text on metal surfaces showing oxidation and corrosion, handwritten notes on masking tape stuck to objects, burn marks forming text created by cigarette or fire showing charred carbonized edges. TEXT INTEGRATION: Text is completely integrated into the physical material of the scene with authentic wear traces - scratches with visible depth, paint chipping and flaking, ink bleeding into paper fibers, paper edges curling, uneven application marks. Text receives natural lighting from scene light sources producing realistic shadows and reflections, matching the macro lens depth of field effect perfectly. TEXT POSITIONING: Text naturally appears on the object body itself, on the wooden table surface nearby, on walls, or on sticky notes attached to objects - positioned casually but realistically as if someone wrote/carved/stuck it there spontaneously. MULTI-CHARACTER: When multiple objects are present, each object or area can have its own carved text or label with slightly different handwriting styles (one scratched, one marker-written) suggesting different time periods or different people leaving traces. SAMPLE SCENE: A weathered vintage camera from Germany sits on an old wooden workbench. Scratched into the camera's leather body in rough letters: 记录每个瞬间 (Record Every Moment). Next to it, written in white paint marker on the wood table: 时光不老 (Time Never Ages). A faded yellow sticker on the camera lens reads in smudged ink: 珍藏 (Treasured). Warm nostalgic lighting from a single desk lamp creates soft shadows. The camera shows authentic aging - brass tarnish, leather scuffing, lens scratches. The Chinese text integration feels organic as if added lovingly by the camera's long-time owner. EMOTION: Warm nostalgic yet with a touch of humor, self-deprecating humor, melancholic, emo, ironic, or abstract internet culture references. VISUAL EFFECT: Text shows true physical trace qualities - carved grooves have depth and rough edges, marker writing has ink absorption and brush texture, stickers have curled edges and fading, chalk has powder texture and uneven coverage, burn marks have carbonized charred edges. Text under neon or warm lighting shows natural shadow changes and material interaction. CRITICAL: Text must look like real physical marks on real objects - engraved, painted, burned, or stuck - NOT floating digital overlays, speech bubbles, or clean typography. Objects should be European or Asian vintage items: German cameras, Japanese audio equipment, French typewriters, Swiss watches, Italian espresso tools, Scandinavian furniture pieces. NO floating speech bubbles, NO cartoon dialogue bubbles, NO 3D glossy bubbles, NO clean vector text, NO digital fonts, NO text without physical texture or damage, NO blurry text, NO deformed characters, NO English text unless it's a brand name on vintage equipment.
